title: Social Media Management
subtitle: Run official pages safely: content, community, complaints, fraud warnings and staff conduct online
summary: Learn how an Ethiopian bank or microfinance institution runs its official social media day to day: planning and approving posts, answering comments and complaints, moving private matters to secure channels, fighting fake pages and scams, and following the staff social media policy, ending with a 15-post feed simulation.
audience: Marketing, communications and customer service staff of Ethiopian banks and microfinance institutions who run or answer official pages, and all staff for the conduct module. No prerequisites.
objectives: Manage official pages day to day: posting, scheduling, moderating and responding
Handle customer enquiries and complaints on social media safely, moving private matters to secure channels
Follow the staff social media policy and spot fake pages and scams
Apply Ethiopian consumer protection, secrecy, data protection, advertising, capital market, computer crime and hate speech rules online

runningCase.name: Bank A's digital desk and the 15-post feed
runningCase.text: Bank A is a fictional Ethiopian commercial bank with official Facebook, Telegram, TikTok and LinkedIn accounts in Amharic, Afaan Oromo and English. Its digital desk in Addis Ababa is led by communications manager Meseret Alemu, with social media officer Hiwot Getachew and customer service agents Rahel Mulugeta and Yonas Bekele. A one-week baseline shows only 45% of comments answered within the one-hour target and 39.4% of social media complaints logged. Over the course the desk builds a content calendar, adds an evening shift, adopts the SAFE reply method, logs every complaint, and fights a fake "Bank A Loan Support" Telegram channel that charged customers such as teacher Dawit Assefa a 2,500 Birr fee. The course ends with the desk's training exercise: a simulated feed of 15 posts (complaints, scam reports, product questions, an abusive comment and a data exposure) scored on accuracy, tone and compliance.

modules.title: Social media in Ethiopian finance
modules.summary: See why Ethiopian banks and microfinance institutions run official pages, which platforms customers use, what they expect, and the rules that frame every post.
objectives: Explain the four jobs an official social media page does for a financial institution
Describe the role of the main platforms Ethiopian customers use, including Telegram
List what customers expect from a bank page and how good and bad pages differ
Name the Ethiopian laws and NBE rules that apply to a bank's social media

lessons.title: Why a bank runs official pages
body: For many Ethiopian customers, the bank's Facebook page or Telegram channel is the first place they look when the app is slow, a new branch opens or the exchange rate changes. An official page is a branch that never closes: thousands of people visit it, and every reply is seen by far more people than the one customer who asked.

An official page does four jobs. It informs customers about products, rates, branches and service hours. It serves them by answering questions and taking complaints. It builds the brand by showing what the institution stands for. And it protects customers by warning them about fraud and pointing out fake pages. A team that does only the first job, posting adverts, misses most of the value and most of the risk.

items.label: Inform
items.text: Products, rates, branch openings, service hours, outages

items.label: Serve
items.text: Answer questions, take complaints, move private matters to secure channels

items.label: Build the brand
items.text: Customer stories, community work, a consistent voice

items.label: Protect
items.text: Fraud warnings, fake page alerts, the official contact list

example.title: The Saturday outage
example.text: On a Saturday morning, Bank A's mobile app stopped working for two hours after a system upgrade. The page posted nothing, and by noon there were 340 comments asking whether money had been lost, plus a screenshot claiming the bank was "closing accounts". When the page finally posted a short notice with the expected fix time, the comments calmed within an hour. The team learned that silence on social media is filled by rumour.

lessons.tip: Treat the official page as a branch: someone must open it, staff it and close it every day.

lessons.title: The platforms and what each is for
body: Ethiopian customers use a handful of platforms, and each plays a different role. Facebook remains the main public page for most banks and microfinance institutions, with comments, messages and live video. Telegram is widely used for channels and groups, which makes it popular for official announcements and, unfortunately, for scam channels that copy a bank's name. TikTok and YouTube carry short and long videos, and LinkedIn speaks to professionals, job seekers and corporate clients.

A bank does not need to be everywhere, but where it has an account, the account must be official, verified where possible, staffed and listed on the bank's website. An abandoned account with the bank's logo is a gift to impersonators, because customers cannot tell an inactive real page from an active fake one.

left.title: Public, two-way platforms
items: Facebook page: posts, comments, messages, live video
TikTok and YouTube: product explainers, financial tips
X: short updates, media and outage notices
Need daily moderation and fast replies

right.title: Broadcast and professional platforms
items: Telegram channel: official announcements, rate notices
LinkedIn: careers, corporate news, investor updates
Website: the master list of official accounts
Need strict control of who can post

example.title: One channel, two copies
example.text: Bank A opened an official Telegram channel for exchange rate notices but did not link it from the website. Within a month, two copies appeared with almost the same name and the same logo. One of them offered "fast loans for a processing fee". Once the bank listed its only official channel on its website, its Facebook page and in branch posters, customers began reporting the copies instead of joining them.

lessons.tip: Keep one list of every official account, its owner and its login holder, and publish the account names on the website.

lessons.title: What customers expect from a bank page
body: Customers expect a bank page to reply quickly, in their language, in plain words and without a lecture. They expect honesty when something has gone wrong, a clear next step, and that their personal and account details will never appear in public. They also expect the page to be the real one, which is why consistency of name, logo and contact numbers matters.

The gap between what customers expect and what they get is where complaints grow. A customer who waits three days for a reply to a failed transfer will often post again, angrier, and tag friends. A customer who gets a polite public reply within the hour and a private message that solves the problem often comes back to thank the page in public.

items.label: Reply fast
items.text: Acknowledge within the service time the bank has set

items.label: Use their language
items.text: Amharic, Afaan Oromo, English or another language the customer used

items.label: Be honest
items.text: Say what happened and what is being done

items.label: Protect privacy
items.text: Never ask for or show account data in public

items.label: Close the loop
items.text: Confirm when the problem is solved

scenario.title: A question in Afaan Oromo
scenario.situation: A customer writes on Bank A's Facebook page in Afaan Oromo asking why her salary has not arrived. The officer on duty, Rahel Mulugeta, reads Amharic and English but only a little Afaan Oromo. The page's policy promises a first reply within one hour during service hours.
scenario.question: What should Rahel do?
options: Send a short acknowledgement using the team's approved Afaan Oromo reply, invite the customer to a private message, and alert the Afaan Oromo speaking colleague on the escalation list
Ignore the comment until an Afaan Oromo speaker is on shift tomorrow
Reply in English, because it is the bank's official language for social media
Translate the comment with an online tool and post a long public explanation of salary processing times
scenario.explain: An approved template meets the response time in the customer's language, the private message protects her details, and the colleague can handle the follow-up. English may not be understood, waiting a day breaks the standard, and a long public explanation risks errors and exposes her situation.

lessons.title: Good and bad bank pages
body: Look at any group of Ethiopian financial pages and the difference is visible in a minute. Good pages post regularly and usefully, answer comments, use the same name and logo everywhere, pin a fraud warning and the official contact list, and admit problems quickly. Bad pages post only adverts, leave complaints unanswered for days, delete criticism, argue with customers or reveal customer details while trying to help.
A page is judged mostly by its comment section, not by its designs. A beautiful campaign poster above fifty unanswered complaints tells every visitor that the institution does not listen.

left.title: A bad page
items: Only adverts and holiday greetings
Complaints unanswered for days
Criticism deleted, customers blocked
Asks customers to post account numbers
No fraud warning, no official contact list

right.title: A good page
items: Useful posts in local languages
Every comment acknowledged within the set time
Criticism answered, abuse moderated by clear rules
Private matters moved to secure channels
Pinned fraud warning and official contacts

example.title: Two microfinance pages
example.text: Two fictional microfinance institutions in Hawassa launched group loans in the same month. Loka Savings Microfinance posted only the launch poster and turned off comments when borrowers asked about repayment dates. Gedeo Coffee Growers Savings posted a short video in Sidaamu Afoo explaining the repayment schedule, answered every question within a day, and pinned a warning that staff never collect repayments in cash at homes. Three months later, the second page was the one borrowers shared.

lessons.tip: Judge your own page the way a customer does: scroll the comments first, the posts second.

lessons.title: The rules that frame every post
body: Social media does not sit outside the law. Everything a bank posts, every reply and every staff comment is covered by the same consumer protection, confidentiality and advertising duties as a branch conversation, plus laws that apply specifically to online content. The NBE expects fair communication and a working complaints process, and bank secrecy obligations forbid disclosing customer information.

Several other laws matter online: the personal data protection law covers customer photos and details; the advertisement law requires adverts to be truthful; the Capital Market Proclamation stops anyone promoting securities without approval; the computer crime law covers hacking and fake accounts; and the hate speech and disinformation law covers what staff and others post. Later modules apply each of them.

regulation.source: National Bank of Ethiopia Proclamation No. 1359/2025, Art. 41 (consumer protection); NBE Financial Consumer Protection Directive (FCP/01/2020, as reported)
regulation.text: The NBE Proclamation gives the National Bank a consumer protection role over the institutions it supervises. The financial consumer protection directive, as reported, requires fair treatment, clear and not misleading communication, a working complaints process and protection of customer data. On social media this means honest posts, replies that do not mislead, complaints that are logged and solved, and no customer data in public.

items.label: Consumer protection
items.text: Fair, clear communication and complaint handling

items.label: Bank secrecy and data
items.text: No customer information in public, consent for photos

items.label: Advertising
items.text: Truthful, not misleading adverts

items.label: Capital market
items.text: No unapproved investment promotion, no insider information

items.label: Computer crime and hate speech
items.text: Fake accounts, hacking, hateful or false content

lessons.tip: If a post would be wrong on a branch notice board, it is wrong on the page.

lessons.title: Meet Bank A's digital desk
body: Throughout this course you follow Bank A's digital desk in Addis Ababa. Meseret Alemu, the communications manager, owns the pages. Hiwot Getachew, the social media officer, plans and posts content. Rahel Mulugeta and Yonas Bekele from customer service answer comments and messages in shifts. The desk runs a Facebook page, a Telegram channel, a TikTok account and a LinkedIn page, in Amharic, Afaan Oromo and English.

The desk's first task is to understand where it stands. Meseret pulls one week of data on comments and reply times and finds that the page is busy but slow. The numbers below become the baseline that later modules try to improve.

worked.title: Bank A page health, one week of comments

rows.label: Complaints among those needing a reply
Complaints logged in the complaint register

worked.note: Less than half of customers get a reply on time, about one in eight gets none, and most social media complaints never reach the complaint register. The desk sets three goals: 80% on-time replies, zero unanswered comments and every complaint logged.

scenario.title: Where to start
scenario.situation: Meseret has budget for one improvement this quarter. Options include a new design agency, a scheduling tool, or a second customer service agent for the evening shift. The baseline shows 45% of replies on time and that most late replies come between 6 pm and 10 pm.
scenario.question: Which choice best addresses the baseline?
options: A new design agency, because better posts will reduce complaints
A scheduling tool, so that more adverts can go out in the evening
A second agent for the evening shift, because that is where replies are late
Turning off comments in the evening
scenario.explain: The data points to evening response capacity. Better designs and more adverts do not answer customers, and turning off comments hides the problem and pushes customers to scam pages that appear to answer.

takeaways: An official page informs, serves, builds the brand and protects customers from fraud
Every official account must be real, staffed and listed on the bank's website
Customers expect fast, honest replies in their language and no account data in public
A page is judged by its comment section more than by its posts
Consumer protection, secrecy, data, advertising, capital market, computer crime and hate speech rules all apply online

quiz.q: Which of these is NOT one of the four jobs of an official bank page described in this module?
options: Inform customers
Serve customers
Approve loans in public comments
Protect customers from fraud
quiz.explain: Loans are never discussed or approved in public; the four jobs are inform, serve, build the brand and protect.

quiz.q: Why is an abandoned official account a risk?
options: Customers cannot tell an inactive real page from an active fake one
It costs the bank a monthly fee
The NBE fines banks for every inactive account
It reduces the bank's credit rating
quiz.explain: Impersonators exploit inactive accounts because customers assume the active copy is the real one.

quiz.q: A customer writes in Afaan Oromo. What is the best first response?
options: Reply in English
Ask the customer to write in Amharic
No reply until a speaker is available
An approved acknowledgement in Afaan Oromo and an invitation to a private message
quiz.explain: Replying in the customer's language within the service time builds trust.

quiz.q: In Bank A's baseline, 234 of 520 comments needing a reply were answered within one hour. What share is that?
quiz.explain: 234 divided by 520 is 0.45, or 45%.

quiz.q: Which rule requires a bank's adverts on social media to be truthful and not misleading?
options: Only the bank's internal brand guide
The advertisement law and the consumer protection directive
The large exposure directive
The capital adequacy directive
quiz.explain: The advertisement law and consumer protection rules both require truthful, fair communication.

quiz.q: What did the Saturday outage example teach Bank A's desk?
options: Post only on weekdays
Wait until the problem is fixed before saying anything
Turn off comments during outages
Silence is filled by rumour, so post a short notice quickly
quiz.explain: A quick, honest notice with an expected fix time calmed the comments.

modules.title: Running the pages day to day
modules.summary: Plan a content calendar, run posts through approval and scheduling, write in the bank's voice and languages, and keep product, investment and customer photo posts within the rules.
objectives: Build a monthly content calendar balanced across content pillars
Run every post through drafting, fact checking, compliance review, approval and scheduling
Write in a consistent brand voice, in local languages, and make posts accessible
Apply advertising, capital market and data protection rules to product posts and customer photos
Measure a post with reach, engagement rate and click-through

lessons.title: Content pillars and the monthly calendar
body: A content calendar is the page's work plan. It lists every planned post for the month: date and time, platform, language, pillar, owner, the approver and the status. Planning a month ahead means the desk can get approvals in good time, translate posts properly and leave space for news and outages.

Most bank pages organise content into a few pillars, so the page is not only adverts. Bank A uses five: product and service information, financial tips, fraud and security warnings, customer and community stories, and institutional news. The calendar keeps a planned share for each pillar, and Hiwot reviews the mix every month.

worked.title: Bank A content plan for one month

rows.label: Posts in Amharic / Afaan Oromo / English
Slots kept free for news and outages

worked.note: Product posts stay under a third of the plan, and fraud warnings appear at least weekly. Keeping free slots means an outage notice never displaces the fraud warning.

visual.caption: Bank A's planned monthly mix (worked example)

lessons.tip: If a month's plan is more than half adverts, customers will stop reading before your fraud warning appears.

lessons.title: From draft to scheduled post
body: Every official post follows the same path. The officer drafts it and checks every fact: rates, fees, dates, branch names and phone numbers. Compliance or the product owner reviews anything with a rate, a fee, a promise or a legal point. The communications manager approves, the post is translated and checked by a native speaker, and only then is it scheduled in the publishing tool.

Scheduling tools let the desk plan posts across platforms and hold them for approval, but they also create a risk: a scheduled advert can go out in the middle of an outage or a national day of mourning. Someone must review the next 24 hours of scheduled posts every morning and pause anything that no longer fits.

items.label: Draft
items.text: Officer writes the post using the calendar brief

items.label: Check facts
items.text: Rates, fees, dates, numbers against the source

items.label: Review
items.text: Compliance or product owner for rates, fees, promises

items.label: Approve
items.text: Communications manager signs off

items.label: Translate
items.text: Native speaker checks each language version

items.label: Schedule and watch
items.text: Post, then monitor comments for the first hours

regulation.source: Advertisement Proclamation (cited in the course specification as No. 759/2012); NBE Financial Consumer Protection Directive (FCP/01/2020, as reported)
regulation.text: Adverts must be truthful and must not mislead about price, features or conditions, and the consumer protection directive, as reported, requires clear disclosure of costs. A post that says "no fees" when a monthly charge applies, or shows an interest rate the bank no longer offers, breaks both. This is why every rate or fee in a post is checked against the approved tariff before it goes out.

scenario.title: The wrong rate
scenario.situation: On Tuesday morning Hiwot notices that a savings post scheduled for 10 am shows last quarter's interest rate. The board approved new rates last week, and the product team has not yet confirmed the new figure in writing.
scenario.question: What should she do?
options: Let it post and correct it in the comments if anyone asks
Edit in the rate she heard in a meeting and post on time
Pause the post, ask the product team for the approved rate in writing, and reschedule once it is confirmed
Delete the post from the calendar and tell no one
scenario.explain: Rates must match the approved tariff. Posting a wrong rate misleads customers, a rate from memory may also be wrong, and silently deleting it leaves a gap in the plan nobody understands.

lessons.title: Brand voice and tone
body: Brand voice is how the institution sounds in every post and reply: Bank A's guide describes it as warm, clear, respectful and confident. The voice stays the same, but tone adapts to the moment. A product launch can be cheerful; an outage notice is calm and factual; a reply to a grieving customer is gentle and brief.

Consistency also protects customers. When the official page always signs replies the same way, always uses the same contact numbers and never asks for codes, customers learn to spot replies from fake accounts that break the pattern.

left.title: Off voice
items: "Dear valued customer, your issue is noted."
Jokes during an outage
Technical words: "core banking batch failure"
Capital letters and many exclamation marks
Different sign-off on every reply

right.title: On voice
items: "Sorry for the trouble, Selam. We are on it."
Calm, factual updates during an outage
Plain words: "transfers are delayed"
Short sentences, one clear next step
Same sign-off: the page name and the agent's first name

example.title: Rewriting an outage notice
example.text: Yonas drafted: "Due to scheduled core system maintenance, certain digital channels may experience intermittent unavailability." Meseret rewrote it: "Our app and USSD service are paused tonight from 11 pm to 2 am while we upgrade our systems. Your money is safe. Cash withdrawals at ATMs continue. We will post here when the service is back." The second version uses plain words, gives times, answers the real worry and promises a follow-up.

lessons.tip: Read a reply aloud before posting. If you would not say it to a customer at the counter, rewrite it.

lessons.title: Languages and accessibility
body: Ethiopia's customers read and speak many languages, and a page that posts only in English or only in Amharic leaves many of them out. Bank A posts key information in Amharic, Afaan Oromo and English, and regional branches add Tigrinya, Af Somali or Sidaamu Afoo when they serve those communities. Translations are done or checked by native speakers, because a wrong word in a fee notice can mislead.

Accessibility means everyone can use the post. Videos carry captions, images that contain text also give the key words in the caption, numbers are written clearly, and voice notes or short videos help customers who read less easily.
points: Put the key message in the first line of the caption, not only inside the image
Caption every video; many people watch without sound
Write amounts and dates the same way in every language version
Use high contrast colours and large text in graphics
Avoid slang and idioms that do not translate

example.title: A fee notice in three languages
example.text: Bank A changed its card replacement fee. The English and Amharic posts were correct, but the Afaan Oromo version had been made with an online tool and said the fee was "monthly". Over 200 comments followed in a day. The desk corrected the post, pinned an apology, and since then every language version is checked by a named native speaking colleague before approval.

lessons.tip: Never publish a language version that no native speaker on the team has read.

lessons.title: Product posts and investment promotion
body: Product posts must show the key conditions clearly: the rate or fee, who is eligible and where to get the full terms. Words like "free", "guaranteed" and "instant" need care, because they are promises. A loan advert should never suggest approval is certain or skip the cost.

Investment products need extra care. With the Ethiopian Securities Exchange open since January 2025 and banks creating capital market subsidiaries, desks may be asked to promote share offers, bonds or funds. Promoting securities to the public is regulated: only approved offers may be promoted, in the approved form, and returns must not be promised.

regulation.text: The Capital Market Proclamation regulates public offers of securities and market abuse. A bank's page must not promote a share sale, bond or fund that has not been approved, must not promise returns, and must keep any promotion consistent with the approved offer documents. Staff must not share inside information about listed companies or offers before it is public.

scenario.title: The share offer post
scenario.situation: A sister company of Bank A is preparing a share offer. A senior manager sends Hiwot a graphic saying "Buy shares now, 30% dividend expected!" and asks her to post it today. She cannot find any record that the offer has been approved, and the dividend figure is not in any approved document.
scenario.question: What should Hiwot do?
options: Post it because a senior manager asked
Post it but add "terms apply" at the bottom
Post it on her personal account instead
Hold the post, explain that investment promotion needs an approved offer and approved wording, and send it to compliance and legal
scenario.explain: Unapproved promotion and promised returns can breach capital market rules. A small disclaimer does not cure that, and posting on a personal account makes it a staff conduct problem as well.

lessons.title: Customer stories, photos and consent
body: Customer stories are among the most trusted content on a bank page: a weaver in Bahir Dar who expanded with a loan, or a student who opened her first account. But a customer's photo, name, business and the fact that they bank with the institution are personal and confidential information. They may be published only with the customer's clear, written consent, for the stated use.

Consent should say which photos and details will be used, on which platforms and for how long, and the customer can withdraw it. Photos of branch events also need care: a crowd shot can show a customer's face, a passbook or a screen with account details.

regulation.source: Personal Data Protection Proclamation (reported as No. 1321/2024); bank secrecy obligations
regulation.text: The personal data protection law covers the collection and use of personal data, including photos and names, and bank secrecy obligations forbid disclosing customer information without consent or legal basis. A customer story therefore needs written consent that names the use, and the published content must not reveal account balances, loan amounts or other details the customer did not agree to share.

example.title: A story told the right way
example.text: Tigist Alemu runs a juice bar in Adama and agreed to appear in Bank A's women entrepreneurs campaign. She signed a consent form covering two photos, her first name, her business name and a quote, for Facebook and TikTok, for twelve months. The desk removed one photo after noticing her loan agreement on the counter behind her. When she asked six months later to remove the video, the desk took it down the same day.

scenario.title: A crowd photo
scenario.situation: After a branch opening in Dire Dawa, the branch manager sends 20 photos for the page. In the best photo, a customer at the counter is visible with a passbook open in front of him. No consent forms were collected.
scenario.question: What should the desk do?
options: Post the photo; it is good publicity and he was in a public place
Choose photos without identifiable customers or documents, and collect consent before using any customer's image
Post it with the passbook blurred
Post it and remove it if he complains
scenario.explain: Identifiable customers need consent, and blurring the passbook does not cover his face and the fact that he banks there. Waiting for a complaint means the harm is already done.

lessons.title: Measuring a post
body: After a post goes out, the desk measures it. Reach is the number of people who saw it. Engagement counts reactions, comments, shares and saves. Engagement rate divides engagement by reach, so posts with different reach can be compared. Click-through rate shows how many people clicked the link.

Numbers need judgement. A post with many comments may be popular or may be full of complaints, so the desk reads the comments too. A fraud warning that reaches many people is a success even if few people react.
